record.original_question: Does the quadratic lower bound lim inf_{T -> +infinity} log P(T) / log T >= 2 hold for every Hamiltonian diffeomorphism on a standard symplectic torus? More generally, does it hold on every aspherical closed symplectic manifold?

evidence.quote: Problem 2.Is it true thatlim inf T→+∞ logP(T) logT ≥2holds for every Hamiltonian diffeo- morphism on a standard symplectic torus? Or in an arbitrary aspherical closed symplectic manifold?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(M,\omega)$ be a closed symplectically aspherical symplectic manifold; that is, $\omega|_{\pi_2(M)}=0$ and $c_1(TM)|_{\pi_2(M)}=0$. For a Hamiltonian diffeomorphism $\varphi\colon M\to M$, let $P(T)$ denote the number of (geometrically distinct) periodic points of $\varphi$ of period at most $T$, i.e. the number of distinct fixed points of the iterates $\varphi^k$ for $1\le k\le T$, counted as orbits.

(a) Is it true that for every Hamiltonian diffeomorphism $\varphi$ of the standard symplectic torus $(\mathbb{T}^{2n},\omega_0)$ one has
$$\liminf_{T\to+\infty}\frac{\log P(T)}{\log T}\ge 2\,?$$

(b) More generally, does the same quadratic lower bound hold for every Hamiltonian diffeomorphism of every closed symplectically aspherical symplectic manifold?
artifact.status_search_result: The Conley conjecture (existence of infinitely many periodic points) is established for symplectically aspherical closed manifolds, and generic lower bounds of order k/log k on the number of periodic orbits are known. However, a uniform quadratic lower bound liminf log P(T)/log T ≥ 2 for every Hamiltonian diffeomorphism on the standard torus, or on arbitrary aspherical closed symplectic manifolds, does not appear to be established in the literature, and the question is posed as an open problem.

status_evidence.title: The Conley Conjecture
status_evidence.snippet: A Hamiltonian diffeomorphism of a closed symplectically aspherical manifold has infinitely many periodic points.
status_evidence.claim: Existence of infinitely many periodic points is known, but the quadratic growth bound is not asserted.

status_evidence.title: Hyperbolic Fixed Points and Periodic Orbits of Hamiltonian Diffeomorphisms
status_evidence.snippet: Generic Hamiltonian diffeomorphism has a simple periodic orbit for every sufficiently large prime period; growth at least k/log k generically.
status_evidence.claim: Only generic and weaker-than-quadratic lower bounds are presently established.
